blurb: Rare brindle hunting dog from Japan's mountains, nicknamed the Tiger Dog
description: The Kai Ken is a rare, medium-sized Japanese hunting dog from Yamanashi with a brindle coat, prick ears and a reputation as agile, alert and loyal to family.
answer: The Kai Ken, also called the Tora Inu or Tiger Dog, is a rare Japanese breed from the Kai region of Yamanashi Prefecture. It is one of six native Japanese breeds protected by the Nihon Ken Hozonkai. It is a medium-sized, brindle-coated hunting dog, typically described as agile, alert and loyal.

body: The Kai Ken was split off from the Nihon Ken landrace when the Nihon Ken Hozonkai (NIPPO) was created in 1928, and is named after Kai Province, where it is said to have originated. It hunted in steep mountain terrain, mainly Japanese serow, deer and wild boar, and occasionally bear. The Kai Ken Aigokai preservation society was formed in 1931, and the breed was designated a national monument of Japan in 1933. It remains rare even in Japan.

It is a medium-sized dog with a wedge-shaped head, prick ears and a tail curled over the back or carried in a sickle. Males typically stand 18 to 22 inches and females 17 to 20 inches. The harsh, medium-length coat comes in shades of brindle: Aka-tora (red), Chu-tora (middle) and Kuro-tora (black). Puppies are born a solid colour, and the stripes can take up to five years to develop fully.

The Kai Ken is commonly described as intelligent, agile, alert and brave, a natural hunter and watchdog that is reserved with strangers but loyal to its family. It is said to be often good with children and not usually aggressive towards other dogs. Many love to swim and have been known to cross rivers and climb trees in pursuit of prey.
Sources give little specific detail on care. Given its history as an agile mountain hunter, it is generally thought to benefit from regular, active exercise.
The source text names no specific health conditions. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: Why is the Kai Ken called the Tiger Dog?
faq.a: Its brindle coat has tiger-like stripes, giving it the name Tora Inu, or Tiger Dog.

faq.q: Are Kai Ken good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as friendly and often good with children, though reserved with strangers.

faq.q: How big does a Kai Ken get?
faq.a: Males typically stand 18 to 22 inches at the shoulder and females 17 to 20 inches.

faq.q: Is the Kai Ken recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is listed as FCI breed number 317 in Group 5, Spitz and Primitive Types.
